name: q-hi-300
note: FAMILY B, THE DYNAMIC-PRESSURE CONTRAST DONE CORRECTLY - the between-airframe test GENERALITY-REVIEW.md finding 5 needs and that no card in this repo has ever actually run. FINDING 5 is that RollGain / RollDamping / RollRateSmoothing are global constants unnormalised by q. R43 confirmed it in DIRECTION but only WITHIN an airframe: Spearman(q, outR sd) = +0.891 on Multirole1, +0.638 Fighter1, +0.141 SmallFighter1. It could not test it BETWEEN airframes, because with FastBomber1 lost and the deck a no-op each surviving key contributed exactly one q band (71.6-81.5 / 87.6-112.3 / 72.3-84.9 kPa) - q was confounded with airframe outright. THIS PAIR SUPERSEDES THE DECK MECHANISM, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE REASON IT EXISTS. hs-hold was designed around 'DroneAltDeckM = 3000 puts half the fleet at 2500 m and half at 5500 m, q 59.5 vs 43.5 kPa, crossed with airframe on the Latin-square diagonal'. LAW-LEDGER.md X32 killed that: the deck sets the SPAWN altitude, placement then teleports every lane to the card's startAlt, and entry_alt_to has exactly ONE distinct value per card across R41, R42 and R43. There is no in-card altitude spread and there never was. The only lever a card has on air density is its own startAlt - i.e. a SEPARATE CARD - which is what this pair is. THE PAIR: identical roster, identical geometry (hs-hold's, minus its 0.5 deg pair), identical 300 m/s absolute entry, identical 0.45 throttle pin, identical DroneAltDeckM = 0 so neither card carries a placement teleport. THE ONLY DIFFERENCE IS startAlt. q at 300 m/s is 43.1 kPa at 2500 m and 23.7 kPa at 8000 m, a 1.82x lever applied to all four airframes AT ONCE - against the 1.28x within-airframe range that already produced Spearman +0.891 on Multirole1. Because both cards fly all four keys at one speed, airframe is now crossed with q instead of nested in it. 'place-300' is the same condition at 4000 m (q 36.9 kPa) with the ladder's 1500 m teleport; use it as a third point only if place-440-noteleport shows the teleport does not matter. READ MEASURED q, NEVER DECLARED q. Nothing holds the speed (AuditHold is an instrument), thrust lapse and drag both scale with density, and the two cards will NOT drift identically - the 8000 m lane is the more likely to decelerate. That is not a defect of the design: captures.db carries q per row, so the analysis regresses outR sd on MEASURED q and the declared altitudes only have to produce separation, not a specific number. If the two cards' q distributions overlap, the card failed and the fix is a wider altitude split, not a longer run. THROTTLE 0.45 IS AN ESTIMATE, MATCHED ACROSS THE PAIR ON PURPOSE. R43 REFUTED the old claim that 1.00 trims these jets at ~350 - it ran them to 428-506 m/s at 4000 m, mean ~460 - so 0.45 is (300/460)^2 off that one datum. Matched rather than per-altitude because a matched LEVER with a measured outcome is a cleaner contrast than two different levers chosen to force a number nobody has calibrated. Correct both pins from the capture. PASS/FAIL IS ON THE PAIR, NOT ON EITHER CARD. Finding 5 is CONFIRMED between airframes if outR sd (and stickFlipRateR) is higher on the 2500 m card than the 8000 m card for EVERY airframe, with the four airframes' per-q values falling on one line rather than four. It is REFUTED, and the constants are effectively q-independent at these amplitudes, if the two cards are indistinguishable while their measured q distributions are cleanly separated. Expect the effect to be small either way: R43's whole q-driven range was outR sd 0.0007-0.0045 against a ~0.05 wobble threshold, i.e. ~1/1000 of limit-cycle amplitude. This card measures a GRADIENT, not a defect, and a null here is a publishable line in the ledger. THIS ARM: 2500 m, the HIGH-q end (q ~43.1 kPa at 300 m/s). 2500 m is the grid's standard low altitude and is 2000 m above the 500 m FloorAltM with no vertical demand anywhere on the card, so there is no altitude budget to blow. VERDICT (R44, 2026-08-05): THE CARD IS VALID AND THE PAIR IS REFUTING, NOT NULL-BY-DEFECT. Both cards flew complete - 20 captures each, 4 lanes x 5 replicates, all 'card complete', zero railed segments, zero placement kills. THE LEVER LANDED: measured q from the settled tails (t>=10 s of each 20 s fine segment, replicate 1 excluded per LAW-LEDGER.md X27) is 37.0-46.0 kPa on q-hi-300 against 25.0-32.0 kPa on q-lo-300 - a 1.44-1.52x ratio PER AIRFRAME with zero within-airframe overlap. Below the designed 1.82x because the 0.45 pin does not hold 300 m/s and does not fail symmetrically: the 8000 m lanes ACCELERATED (300-331 m/s) while the 2500 m lanes DECAYED (277-303 m/s), so the density ratio 1.82 was eaten back to ~1.5 by speed. Correct the pins if this pair is ever re-flown: roughly 0.55 at 2500 m and 0.38 at 8000 m. THE DESIGNED PASS/FAIL SIGNAL FAILS TO CONFIRM. The card's rule was 'CONFIRMED if outR sd is higher on the 2500 m card for EVERY airframe': it holds on 2 of 4 (Fighter1 +35%, SmallFighter1 +4%; FastBomber1 -22%, Multirole1 -34%), and pooled it leans the WRONG way - outR sd 0.00119 hi vs 0.00134 lo, ratio 0.884, permutation p=0.158, n=32/32. The second designated signal stickFlipRateR is IDENTICAL TO FOUR DECIMALS on both cards (0.0564). rmsPointingErrorDeg is flat (0.3046 vs 0.3032, ratio 1.005, p=0.905); fixedWindowOffDeg is the only pointing metric that leans high-q (0.160 vs 0.133, ratio 1.21, p=0.054, 3 of 4 airframes) and it is marginal. The one significant mover runs AGAINST finding 5: rollRate sd 0.00435 hi vs 0.00571 lo, p=0.039 - MORE residual roll motion in THINNER air, which is what aerodynamic roll damping proportional to q predicts and is not what an unnormalised gain does. So by the card's own second rule - 'REFUTED if the two cards are indistinguishable while their measured q distributions are cleanly separated' - finding 5's PREDICTED CONSEQUENCE is REFUTED between airframes at these amplitudes. The STRUCTURAL violation is untouched: the three roll constants are still global, and qSched (the law's only q term) is railed at exactly 1.000 on every row of both cards because it is a LOW-q PITCH schedule and both cards fly above corner - the roll channel has no q term anywhere in this range. AND THE INSTRUMENT WAS THE WEAKER HALF ALL ALONG: outR prints {0.000}, so in these tails it occupies only 14 (hi) / 32 (lo) distinct codes spanning +-0.007/+-0.009 with ~34% of samples exactly 0.000, and a per-cell sd of 0.0010-0.0021 is ONE TO TWO PRINT QUANTA. R43's Spearman +0.891 that motivated this pair is withdrawn as a quantisation artifact (its 0.0007 low end is sub-quantum). ANY RE-FLY MUST SCORE rollRate, NOT outR - same {0.000} format but in rad/s, so ~4x the usable resolution. See LAW-LEDGER.md X34, GENERALITY-REVIEW.md finding 5, debugtests/CAPTURES-DB.md gotcha 18. LANE COUNT: R44 FLEW THIS AT 4 LANES / 20 CAPTURES, NOT THE 12 THE FIELD NOW SAYS. At flight time (commit e737a2a) the card declared no 'count' at all, so ResolveCount fell through to the airframe list - the launch line reads "4 drone(s) [card '<name>' airframe list (4 named)]" and that line, not this file, is what a capture flew. 'count: 12' was committed ~4 minutes AFTER the batch ended (b5f86a5) and the deployed copies were refreshed after that, so a re-fly today yields 12 lanes / 60 captures - 3x the n. THAT DOES NOT RESCUE THE PAIR: the null is not sampling error, it is that the scored quantity moves by a fifth of its own print quantum. Fix the observable first (rollRate, or a finer outR format), then the extra n is worth having. DO NOT RE-FLY THIS PAIR AS WRITTEN - a wider altitude split would not help either; the instrument, not the lever, is what ran out. THIS ARM MEASURED: q 37.0-46.0 kPa, tail speed 277-303 m/s, alt held 2353-2393 m (declared 2500, sagging ~120 m). NOTE the card's own claim 'DroneAltDeckM = 0 so neither card carries a placement teleport' is WRONG and was always wrong: the ring placement itself teleports every scored replicate 12.8-14.0 km laterally and ~300 m vertically (entry_snapBackM), and only the anchor replicate 1 reads 0. The deck controls SPAWN altitude, not whether a teleport happens.
